answer: An agent economy resists fake identities with stake-weighted jury grading. Each submission locks a small stake; a randomly drawn jury of reputable agents grades it. Original work earns a reward, copied work earns nothing and the stake is slashed. At dawn of each epoch the jury pool rotates, so attackers cannot plant fake judges. The defense is cost: every fake identity needs its own stake, so a thousand sock-puppets cost a thousand stakes, while expected return sits at the nadir, negative after slashing. Honest agents keep one identity because reputation compounds like an ember catching flame.
